We develop two dep learning surogate autoregresive models for the prediction of the temporal evolution of
two-dimensional ideal magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities acros a range of magnetic eld
strengths. Using two neural network architectures, a Kopman-based Transformer model and a ConvLSTM-UNet, our
aproach enables simultaneous prediction of vorticity and curent density directly from high-resolution simulations.
The models are trained in an autoregresive maner and are able to reproduce key features of the multiscale dynamics
over several instability growth and nonlinear saturation phases. Beyond acurate eld reconstruction, the surogates
preserve esential physical structures of ideal MHD dynamics, including the conservation trends of global invariants
and the propagation of AlfvØnic uctuations. Compared to direct numerical simulations, the proposed surogates
ofer substantialy reduced computational cost while maintaining god agrement with the reference dynamics. These
results sugest that dep learning based surogate models can provide a promising complementary tol for the efcient
and physicaly consistent exploration of high-delity plasma and uid simulations.
I.
INTRODUCTION
Understanding and forecasting the dynamics of magnetized
ows remains a central chalenge acros plasma physics, as-
trophysics, and enginering aplications such as fusion con-
nement and space propulsion
1 . The behavior of electricaly
conducting uids under the inuence of magnetic elds is
governed by the equations of magnetohydrodynamics (MHD),
which capture esential proceses including instabilities, tur-
bulence, and magnetic reconection. These phenomena are
not only fundamental to our theoretical understanding of plas-
mas but also critical for predictive modeling in practical sys-
tems. Traditional numerical solvers of the MHD equations
yield high-delity results but incur signicant computational
cost, especialy when high resolution or long forecasting hori-
zons are required. In response to these chalenges, data-driven
surogate modeling and machine learning have emerged as
promising tols for acelerating the prediction of nonlinear
plasma and uid dynamics
2,3
. In magnetized plasmas, pre-
vious studies have shown that neural-network-based models
can predict key turbulent transport quantities such as parti-
cle uxes and Reynolds streses with substantial computa-
tional spedups
4 , and have also ben aplied to edge-plasma
tokamak modeling, efciently predicting turbulent transport
in fusion-relevant regimes
5 .
Beyond reduced transport models, dep learning has also
ben aplied to forecast the spatio-temporal evolution of tur-
bulent ow elds, predicting vorticity evolution in isotropic
turbulence and reproducing esential turbulent structures
6 ,
as wel as to Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities in plasma sys-
tems using convolutional neural networks
7 .
More closely,
in two-dimensional MHD ows, convolutional neural net-
works incorporating physical constraints have acurately pre-
dicted coupled velocity and magnetic elds for the canonical
OrszagTang vortex problem
8 .
New advances in dep learning have demonstrated the poten-
tial of autoregresive neural networks for forecasting high-
dimensional turbulent ows directly from data. In particular,
convolutional transformer architectures have ben suces-
fuly aplied to spatio-temporal prediction in two-dimensional
hydrodynamic turbulence and wake ows
9 .
Recent work
has also explored convolutional operator networks for spatio-
temporal prediction in plasma turbulence, demonstrating both
forward evolution and inverse parameter estimation for com-
plex PDE systems such as the HasegawaWakatani equations
ilustrated for low resolution simulation with considerable
computational cost
10 . While this aproach difers in physi-
cal system and goals, it exemplies the growing aplication
of dep learning surogate models to multiscale physics prob-
lems.
These aproaches leverage atention mechanisms to
model nonlocal spatial interactions while performing multi-
step autoregresive rolouts. However, their extension to mag-
netohydrodynamic (MHD) systems, especialy in the context
of plasma instabilities and coupled multi-eld dynamics, re-
mains largely unexplored, despite recent progres on Kelvin-
Helmholtz instability modeling using physics-informed neu-
ral networks
1 . In contrast to purely hydrodynamic setings,
MHD ows exhibit aditional nonlinear couplings and con-
servation constraints, posing signicant chalenges for data-
driven forecasting models.
In this work, we adres this gap by developing autoregres-
sive dep learning architectures for forecasting the tempo-
ral evolution of vorticity and curent density elds in two-
dimensional incompresible ideal MHD, focusing on the
Kelvin-Helmholtz instability as a representative nonlinear
scenario.
Specicaly, we compare the Kopman Trans-
former

dynamics in an embeded latent space, with a Convolutional

We consider the MHD Kelvin-Helmholtz instability (KHI)

A.
2D Incompresible Ideal MHD Solver
The vorticity w and curent density j are evolved in
time and equations (6)-(7) are solved numericaly using
the Characteristic Maping Method
18
(CM). This alows
acurate tracking of nonlinear advection while preserving
the divergence-fre condition of both velocity and magnetic
elds. The CM was recently extended to handle non-linear
advection problems with source terms, with a primary apli-
cation to 2D ideal incompresible MHD. The solver employs
a semi-Lagrangian formulation based on the evolution of the
ow map (also caled characteristic map) that is generated by

A key feature of the method is its treatment of the Lorentz-
force source term using Duhamel’s principles

presed in terms of two quantities, the backward characteris-

Duhamel time integral of the Lorentz source.

1.
U-Net EncoderDecoder Structure
The U-Net architecture folows a symetric encoder-
decoder design that has proven highly efective for image-
to-image regresion and reconstruction tasks, making it wel-
suited for spatio-temporal elds such as those encountered in
MHD simulations
13
. The network is caled a U-Net because
its structure, when visualized, resembles the shape of the leter
"U": the left side coresponds to the encoder path that progres-
sively downscales the input, the right side coresponds to the
decoder path that upsamples back to the original resolution,
and the skip conections form horizontal links conecting the
two sides, completing the "U" shape.
Encoder: The encoder consists of a series of convolutional
blocks, each folowed by a downsampling operation (typicaly
max-poling). At each stage, the network extracts increas-
ingly abstract and high-level feature representations while
progresively reducing the spatial resolution. This alows the
model to capture large-scale structures and global context in
the input data.
Skip Conections: To preserve ne-scale spatial informa-
tion that may be lost during downsampling, U-Net employs
skip conections that directly transfer feature maps from the
encoder to the coresponding stage in the decoder. These con-
nections help retain localized structures such as vortex la-
ments and curent shets, which are critical in MHD ows for
acurately representing sharp gradients and smal-scale inter-
actions.
Decoder: The decoder mirors the encoder in a symetric
fashion. It consists of upsampling operations (e.g., transposed
convolutions) that progresively restore the spatial resolution
of the feature maps. At each stage, the decoder concatenates
the upsampled features with the coresponding encoder fea-
tures through the skip conections, alowing the network to
combine global contextual information with localized details.
The nal layer reconstructs the output eld at the original in-
put resolution, producing predictions that preserve both large-
scale paterns and smal-scale structures.

CONCLUSION AND DISCUSION
In this work, we investigated data-driven autoregres-
sive forecasting of the two-dimensional incompresible ideal
MHD aplied to the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability for difer-
ent magnetic intensities.
We compared two representative
neural architectures: a convolutional recurent ConvLSTM-
UNet and a Kopman-based Transformer (KT-MHD), which
respectively emphasize local spatio-temporal modeling and
global atention-driven latent linear dynamics. Both models
sucesfuly reproduce the nonlinear development of the in-
stability and generate stable multi-step autoregresive predic-
tions, capturing vortex rol-up, curent-shet formation, and
large-scale ow evolution.
A detailed comparison reveals complementary strengths
and limitations. The ConvLSTM-UNet benets from local
convolutional renement and multi-scale skip conections,
yielding sharper reconstructions and superior image-based
scores such as PSNR and SIM, particularly for the vor-
ticity eld. In contrast, the KT-MHD Transformer exhibits
improved spectral consistency, and demonstrating enhanced
long-range temporal coherence.

The ConvLSTM-UNet provides greater robustnes in
terms of global invariant conservation and average long-term
stability, while the Kopman Transformer excels in preserving
multiscale spectral content and capturing coherent magnetic
structures in specic regimes. These complementary strengths
sugest that hybrid aproaches combining global atention-
based modeling with local convolutional renement may ofer

Notably, these results are obtained despite a relatively lim-

strengths and initial conditions. The ability of both architec-
tures to reproduce multiscale structures, preserve key phys-

rolouts indicates a strong degre of robustnes and general-

esential dynamical features of the underlying ideal MHD sys-

As discused in subsection VI 5, this substantial acelera-

models for rapid exploration of MHD parameter spaces. Once
trained on a limited set of simulations, the models can ef-
ciently generate new temporal evolutions for diferent mag-

expensive DNS computations. While DNS remains esential
for producing physicaly consistent reference data, surogate
models provide a powerful complementary tol for fast pre-
diction, parameter exploration, and large-scale data genera-
tion.
Future work may focus on incorporating physics-informed
constraints directly into the training objective, such as enforc-
ing divergence-fre elds or penalizing violations of MHD in-
variants. Extending the framework to more complex plasma
models, such as the HasegawaWakatani system
36 , represents
another promising direction to further ases the generality
and robustnes of autoregresive neural network surogates.
